items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: I would go into Boston, and go jamming with Sabby Lewis, who had a famous band

ctx.x: From the tuba to the trombone?

Yes, from the tuba to the trombone, was in 19 — I went into the Navy in 1942, so this was like 1939. And so I wanted to play in the band because they had all these great musicians: Clark Terry and Osie Johnson and Dudley Brooks and all these famous musicians, but they wouldn’t let me in because they were using the string bass now. And so I would get up and go into the head in the morning and start practicing on the trombone because it was a bass clef instrument, and finally, one of the guys went over the hill one…

getting pretty good with the trombone. But then the sailors that we had in Hingham from being not able to read or write and like that, they were contained like in the department where they didn’t have no — to go out on liberty as it was called. See they had to stay there and so they got jealous of the band. See they can go out and everything, and would you believe they changed it around and wanted the band to go out there and do this work. And here the saxophone players with the fingers and everything, so we…
